ai.title: CLI landing screen layout tweaks and Kimi tagline update
ai.summary: Freebuff CLI landing screen logic now conditionally renders streak bonus notes and logos based on terminal dimensions to prevent UI crowding. The `getFreebuffStreakBonusNoteForLayout` function suppresses the note if height < 52 or width is insufficient, while logo display rules shift to hide branding in medium-height terminals unless the picker is collapsed. ai.title: Base2 agent caps thinker spawns at one per request
ai.summary: Base2 agent prompt injects `THINKER_SPAWN_LIMIT` constant into spawn, core, and implementation sections. Restricts thinker agent spawning to one per user request to prevent redundant agent invocations. Applies to `agents/base2/base2.ts` across default, free, lite, max, and fast modes. Constant enforces 'do not spawn any thinker again' after first spawn.

eli5.text: A helper mode within the assistant now starts at most one deep-reasoning sub-agent per question you ask. Previously it could spin up several of these sub-agents at once; now it stops itself after the first one, which should keep responses a bit more focused. The change applies to everyone using that assistant mode today.

The instruction that told it how many sidekicks to call in was moved to a new spot in its internal checklist, right after the note reminding it to keep prompts short. facts: Prefer the server-sent limit (base + streak/referral bonuses) so the counter and its amber exhausted cue match what admission will enforce; the static constants only cover the pre-snapshot fallback.
No queued state any more: there's never a model the user is "already in" the queue for, so re-picking is always meaningful.

The pool resets daily on a Pacific-day boundary regardless of usage, so the countdown is meaningful even at zero used, getFreebuffPremiumResetAt falls back to the next day boundary when the server hasn't sent a resetAt yet.

With the shared premium pool spent, rejoining on the still-selected premium model would be rejected server-side and dead-end on the terminal rate-limited screen. Continue on the unlimited fallback (DeepSeek V4 Flash) instead, the same flip the landing picker's recommendation makes.
Limited tier is excluded: its models all share the one exhausted pool, so there is nothing to flip to.
entries.title: CLI update: freebuff-landing-screen
entries.summary: CLI, Shared/Core changes across 4 file(s) (+132/−71).

ai.title: MiniMax M3 joins premium pool with auto-flip to fallback when
ai.summary: MiniMax M3 is now a premium model, so it draws from the shared 5/day premium pool instead of being unlimited. The `premium` flag on MINIMAX_M3_MODEL flipped from false to true in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts, and FREEBUFF_MINIMAX_M3_MODEL_ID was added to FREEBUFF_PREMIUM_MODEL_IDS. The same module's `getRecommendedFreebuffModelId` takes a `premiumExhausted` option, which the model selector and landing screen pass from the live quota snapshot so the recommended hero flips to the unlimited DeepSeek V4 Flash when the pool runs out. The session-ended banner performs a related in-memory flip: when the selected model is premium and the pool is exhausted, pressing Enter rejoins on FALLBACK_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID instead of reposting a model the server would reject. The landing screen and collapsed picker now read `sessionRateLimit?.limit` before falling back to the static FREEBUFF_PREMIUM_SESSION_LIMIT or FREEBUFF_LIMITED_SESSION_LIMIT, so the counter and the amber exhausted cue match what admission enforces.
ai.evidence: common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts flips MINIMAX_M3_MODEL `premium` from false to true and adds FREEBUFF_MINIMAX_M3_MODEL_ID to FREEBUFF_PREMIUM_MODEL_IDS; cli/src/components/session-ended-banner.tsx adds continueOnFallback logic that flips the rejoin model to FALLBACK_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID when the selected model is premium and the pool is exhausted; cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx and freebuff-landing-screen.tsx pass premiumExhausted into getRecommendedFreebuffModelId and prefer sessionRateLimit?.limit over the static FREEBUFF_PREMIUM_SESSION_LIMIT/FREEBUFF_LIMITED_SESSION_LIMIT fallback.
ai.migration: If you normally start chats on MiniMax M3, you will now consume one of the 5 daily premium sessions instead of an unlimited slot.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show whether MiniMax M3 was previously treated as unlimited for quota purposes before this commit.

changes.what: Sets MINIMAX_M3_MODEL premium to true and adds FREEBUFF_MINIMAX_M3_MODEL_ID to FREEBUFF_PREMIUM_MODEL_IDS, making MiniMax M3 part of the shared daily premium pool.
Passes premiumExhausted from the live rate-limit snapshot into getRecommendedFreebuffModelId so the recommended hero flips to the unlimited fallback when the pool is spent.
Adds continueOnFallback logic that flips the rejoin model to FALLBACK_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID in memory when the selected model is premium and the pool is exhausted.

Reads sessionRateLimit?.limit before the static FREEBUFF_PREMIUM_SESSION_LIMIT and FREEBUFF_LIMITED_SESSION_LIMIT fallback so the session counter and amber exhausted cue match server-enforced admission.

ai.title: Freebuff daily session limit raised from 5 to 6
ai.summary: The default daily free-session quota for both full and limited access tiers moved from 5 to 6 in `FREEBUFF_PREMIUM_SESSION_LIMIT` and `FREEBUFF_LIMITED_SESSION_LIMIT` inside `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, which the landing screen's pre-snapshot fallback and the "0 of N … used" hint reference in `cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx`. A type doc comment in `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts` was reworded to drop the hardcoded "5/day premium" example. There are three accompanying comment-only changes across the model and session constants modules.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, `FREEBUFF_PREMIUM_SESSION_LIMIT` and `FREEBUFF_LIMITED_SESSION_LIMIT` both changed from 5 to 6; the same 5→6 change is reflected in the limited-mode FAQ of `README.md` and `freebuff/cli/release/README.md`; the comment on `REFERRAL_CLI_DAILY_SESSION_BONUS_CAP` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-referral-tiers.ts` was reworded to match (6 base + 3 = 9/day); and `cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx` updated the counter fallback and "0 of N" comment to the new limit.

ai.title: CLI release package version bump to 0.0.127
ai.summary: freebuff/cli/release/package.json version bumped from 0.0.126 to 0.0.127. Internal packaging update for the CLI release artifact. No functional changes or user-facing impact.

eli5.text: Nothing for you to see or do here. Behind the scenes, the packaging label on the free coding agent was ticked up one small step so that automated installs keep pulling the current build. The version number changed, but no features did. The version label was updated from 0.0.126 to 0.0.127; that alone is internal packaging with no user-visible change. What this label carries is the prior release content already in your hands: Premium and limited sessions now allow one more item in a row (the cap went up by one), the assistant's landing screen got small layout tweaks and a refreshed tagline, and a couple of internal limits were nudged (the streak bonus minimum height was lowered and thinker spawns are now capped at one per request). Those changes shipped before, so updating to this label gives you no new behavior, only the current packaged build. It is live today; if you reinstalled now you'd receive the same experience you already have.
